scenarios.name: update-ok-control
scenarios.why: no fault: the success path on the same row and COMMAREA as the faulted scenarios, so each fault is read against it

scenarios.name: update-fails-904
scenarios.why: UPDATE of ACCOUNT fails -904 (resource unavailable): the SQLCODE NOT = 0 arm after the UPDATE -- 'N' in COMM-SUCCESS, the 'ERROR: UPDACC returned -904 on UPDATE' DISPLAY, GO TO UAD999, the row untouched and the COMMAREA not refilled

scenarios.name: update-fails-913
scenarios.why: UPDATE fails -913 (deadlock / timeout): the same arm with the other SQLCODE the CBSA programs abend on elsewhere

scenarios.name: update-fails-803
scenarios.why: UPDATE fails -803 (duplicate key): the same arm, a third SQLCODE (the UPDATE touches no key column, so -803 is not one Db2 gives, but the program's test is NOT = 0)

scenarios.name: select-fails-904
scenarios.why: SELECT INTO fails -904: the arm after the SELECT -- 'N', 'ERROR: UPDACC returned -904 on SELECT', GO TO UAD999, no UPDATE run

scenarios.name: select-fails-913
scenarios.why: SELECT INTO fails -913: the same arm, the other SQLCODE; the table is compared and no UPDATE ran

scenarios.name: blank-account-type
scenarios.why: a blank account type: 'N' without the UPDATE, so the UPDATE arms above are read against a run that never reaches them

scenarios.name: account-not-found
scenarios.why: SELECT +100 (no such account): 'N', 'ERROR: UPDACC returned +100 on SELECT', no UPDATE -- the SELECT arm taken by Db2, not by an injected fault

notes: UPDACC with SQL faults injected (#4507, [c:e095a6ab]): the UPDATE (line 278) and SELECT (line 191) failure arms of CBSA's update-account service on UPDACC's own CRETB01/CREI101 DDL and the hand case's seed. cbsa-updacc and cbsa-updacc-generated run the model-written port, which reaches Db2 through JDBC rather than cobolrt.sql.DetSql, so the proof refuses a sql_faults scenario there ("no SQL fault hook in UPDACC"); this case has no port/ directory, so the deterministic translation runs and the seam exists. The statement is addressed by line (the precompiled COBOL source line) and each SQLCODE is compared with GnuCOBOL plus the stub; the table is compared after every scenario.
